text:
At the foot of the mountains, on the edge of a village, lived an old man named Rustam. The whole village came to him for advice, because he knew life well and never spoke in haste.

The old man had a grandson named Behzod, a boy of twelve. Behzod was a good boy, but lately something inside him had changed. Sometimes he got angry and fought with his friends. Sometimes he felt envious and couldn’t be happy for other people’s success. And sometimes he felt worthless and didn’t want to talk to anyone.

One evening, as they sat by the fire, Behzod came to his grandfather and lowered his head.

“Grandfather,” he said, “today at school I got into a fight with Jasur. He hadn’t actually done anything. On the exam, I got a worse grade, and he got the top mark. And a terrible feeling rose up in me. Why did I behave like that? I’m ashamed of myself.”

Grandfather Rustam sat quietly, looking into the fire. Then he said softly:

“My grandson, let me tell you something. Inside you, and inside me, and inside every person, live two wolves, and they are always fighting each other.”

Behzod looked up in surprise. “Wolves? Inside me?”

“Yes,” said the old man. “The first wolf is evil. He is made of anger, envy, selfishness, pride, and fear. He always complains, always blames others, always demands more. His voice is loud and sharp.

The second wolf is good. He is made of love, patience, humility, honesty, and hope. He rejoices in others’ happiness, admits his mistakes, and chooses the right path even in hard times. His voice is quiet and calm.”

Behzod thought it over. The fire crackled. Then he asked eagerly:

“Grandfather, if they fight, which one wins?”

Grandfather Rustam smiled and looked at his grandson warmly.

“The one you feed.”

Behzod didn’t understand. “What does it mean to feed them, Grandfather?”

“You see,” said the old man, “every wolf needs food to gain strength. If you give in to bad thoughts, if you shout when you’re angry, if you keep envy inside you, you are feeding the first wolf. He grows fat and strong. And one day he will take complete control of you.

But if you are kind, if you learn to forgive, if you share in others’ joy, if you do good deeds, you are feeding the second wolf. He grows stronger and shows you the right path.”

Behzod sat silent for a long time, thinking about his grandfather’s words. Then he said in a calmer voice, “Grandfather, I’m ashamed that I spoke harshly to Jasur. May I apologize to him tomorrow?”

“You may, my grandson,” said the old man. “Just now, you fed the second wolf.”

The next morning, Behzod arrived at school early and met Jasur. With his head bowed, he said, “I’m sorry about yesterday. You did well fairly, and I congratulate you on your grade.”

Jasur was surprised, then smiled broadly. “It’s all right. I lost my temper too. Let’s prepare together, and next time we’ll both get top marks.”

From that day on, Behzod asked himself every day: “Which wolf did I feed today?” Sometimes the evil wolf won, sometimes the good one. But Behzod got up each morning and tried again. Years passed, and Behzod grew into a kind, honest, and strong man. The whole village respected him.

Moral: Good and evil struggle inside each of us. Which one wins is decided not by fate but by your daily choices. Whatever you feed will grow. So every day, ask yourself: “Which wolf did I feed today?”

tr.title: Ikki bo’ri
paragraphs: Tog’lar bag’rida, qishloq chekkasida keksa bir bobo yashar ekan. Uning ismi Rustam bobo ekan. Butun qishloq unga maslahat so’rab kelar, chunki u hayotni yaxshi bilar, hech qachon shoshilib gapirmas ekan.

Boboning Behzod ismli nevarasi bor ekan. U o’n ikki yoshli bola ekan. Behzod yaxshi bola ekan, lekin so’nggi paytlarda uning ichida nimadir o’zgarib qolgan ekan. Ba’zan jahli chiqib, do’stlari bilan urishib qolar, ba’zan hasad qilib, boshqalarning yutug’iga quvona olmas ekan. Ba’zan esa o’zini hech narsaga yaramaydigandek his qilib, hech kim bilan gaplashgisi kelmas ekan.
Bir kuni kechqurun, olov yonida o’tirganlarida, Behzod bobosining yoniga kelib, boshini quyi solibdi.

«Bobo», debdi u. «Bugun maktabda Jasur bilan urishib qoldim. Aslida u hech narsa qilmagan edi. Shunchaki imtihondan men yaxshi baho olmagan joyda, u a’lo baho olgan edi. Menda shunday yomon his paydo bo’ldi. Men nega bunday bo’ldim? O’zimdan o’zim uyalaman.»
Rustam bobo olovga qarab, bir oz jim o’tiribdi. Keyin ohista debdi:
«Nevaram, men senga bir narsa aytib beray. Sening ichingda ham, mening ichimda ham, har bir odamning ichida ikkita bo’ri yashaydi, ular bir-biri bilan doim jang qilib turadi.»
Behzod ajablanib bosh ko’taribdi. «Bo’rilar? Mening ichimdami?»

«Ha», debdi bobo. «Birinchi bo’ri yomon bo’ri. U g’azab, hasad, xudbinlik, g’urur va qo’rquvdan iborat. U doim shikoyat qiladi, doim boshqalarni ayblaydi, doim ko’proq narsa talab qiladi. Uning ovozi baland va o’tkir.

Ikkinchi bo’ri yaxshi bo’ri. U mehr, sabr, kamtarlik, halollik va umiddan iborat. U boshqalarning quvonchiga quvonadi, xatolarini tan oladi, qiyin paytda ham to’g’ri yo’lni tanlaydi. Uning ovozi ohista va tinch.»
Behzod bir muddat o’ylab qolibdi. Olov chirsillab yonar ekan. Keyin u shoshib so’rabdi:
«Bobo, ular jang qilsa, qaysi biri g’olib chiqadi?»
Rustam bobo jilmayib, nevarasiga mehr bilan qarabdi.
«Qaysi birini boqsang, o’sha g’olib chiqadi.»
Behzod bu gapni tushunib yetmabdi. «Boqish nima degani, bobo?»

«Ko’ryapsanmi», debdi bobo. «Har bir bo’ri kuch olish uchun ovqatga muhtoj. Sen yomon fikrlarga berilsang, jahling kelganda ichingdan baqirsang, hasadni o’z ichingda saqlasang, birinchi bo’rini boqqan bo’lasan. U semirib, kuchayib boradi. Shunda bir kun kelib, u seni to’liq egallab oladi.
Sen mehrli bo’lsang, kechirishni o’rgansang, boshqalarning quvonchiga sherik bo’lsang, yaxshi ishlarni qilsang, ikkinchi bo’rini boqqan bo’lasan. U kuchayadi va senga to’g’ri yo’lni ko’rsatadi.»
Behzod bobosining so’zlarini o’ylab, uzoq jim o’tiribdi. Keyin kechirimli ovozda debdi: «Bobo, men Jasurga qattiq gapirganim uchun uyalaman. Ertaga undan uzr so’rasam bo’ladimi?»
«Bo’ladi, nevaram», debdi bobo. «Mana, sen hozirning o’zida ikkinchi bo’rini boqding.»
Ertasiga ertalab Behzod maktabga erta borib, Jasurni kutib olibdi. Boshini egib: «Kecha uchun uzr, sen to’g’ri ish qilgansan, imtihondagi bahoing bilan tabriklayman», debdi.
Jasur ajablanibdi, keyin keng jilmayibdi. «Hechqisi yo’q. Mening ham jahlim chiqib ketgan edi. Keling, birga tayyorlanamiz, keyingi safar ikkalamiz ham a’lo baho olamiz.»

Shu kundan boshlab Behzod har kuni o’zidan so’rar ekan: «Bugun qaysi bo’rini boqdim?» Ba’zan yomon bo’ri g’alaba qilar, ba’zan yaxshi bo’ri. Lekin Behzod ertalab turib, yana yangidan urinib ko’rar ekan. Yillar o’tib, Behzod mehribon, halol va kuchli inson bo’lib yetishibdi. Uni butun qishloq hurmat qilar ekan.

Qissadan hissa: Har birimizning ichimizda yaxshilik va yomonlik kurashayotgan bo’ladi. Qaysi biri g’alaba qilishini taqdir emas, sening kundalik tanlovlaring hal qiladi. Qaysi fikrni boqsang, o’sha o’sadi. Shuning uchun har kuni o’zingdan so’ra: «Bugun qaysi bo’rini boqdim?»

quiz.q: Behzod got into a fight with Jasur at school.
The evil wolf has a quiet and calm voice.
What did Behzod do the next morning?
